title: Blaze breaks out at Trafford suspected illegal waste dump

input.lead: A fire broke out at a suspected illegal waste site near Carrington Spur in Trafford, Greater Manchester
input.summary: A fire broke out at a suspected illegal waste site near Carrington Spur in Trafford, Greater Manchester
input.evidence_text: Blaze breaks out at Trafford suspected illegal waste dump - BBC News Image caption, Fire crews wearing breathing apparatus tackled the blaze close to the River Mersey near the Carrington Spur By Richard Stead North West Published 10 August 2026 Firefighters have been tackling a blaze at a suspected illegal waste dump close to the River Mersey in Greater Manchester. Crews were called to the scene at 11:30 BST on Monday after reports that smoke had been coming from the site in woodland close to the Carrington Spur. Helen Carr from Flixton, who walks her dogs in woodland nearby, said: "The smell is absolutely acrid and what I really worry about is things like builders' waste setting on fire, then releasing all sorts of chemicals into the air. "Its criminal. There is just no need for people to be dumping waste like this, in this day and age. This is just sheer greed and laziness." Image caption, Helen Carr said she was concerned about the waste being dumped at the site The 43 year-old added: "The type of rubbish being dumped used to be agricultural waste, but it now involves builders waste alongside household waste, with things like mattresses and fridge freezers. "The waste has just being growing and growing and getting out of control." In July, Ms Carr reported the waste to the Environment Agency (EA), which responded by saying they were aware of the site and has referred the case to the Area Enforcement Team. In an email to Ms Carr, the EA said: "We take illegal waste offences seriously and will use the powers available to us to investigate and, where appropriate, take enforcement action against those responsible." He was also convicted of four counts of indecent assault and one count of indecency of a child between 1997 and 2001. title: Conflict ruling hits plans for Greater Manchester's tallest tower

input.lead: The development, which would reshape skyline with a 78-storey skyscraper, must return to a planning panel
input.summary: The development, which would reshape skyline with a 78-storey skyscraper, must return to a planning panel
input.evidence_text: Plans to build Greater Manchester's tallest tower have suffered a setback after a planning approval process was ruled to have been affected by a conflict of interest Henley Investment Management secured approval last November for plans to partly demolish Regent Retail Park and build about 3,300 homes across 10 buildings. The development would include a 78-storey skyscraper, making it the tallest building in the region The scheme was approved despite opposition from more than 460 residents, who raised concerns about over-development and pressure on local infrastructure Objections were also lodged by Salford MP Rebecca Long-Bailey and several current and former councillors However, the approval process is now set to be reconsidered after a complaint by the Save Regent Retail Park campaign group was upheld by Salford City Council's legal department The complaint found there had been a "procedural conflict of interest" involving councillor Philip Cusack, then chair of the planning committee, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said

input.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

input.evidence_text: Wigan Museum will close from 25 July while new exhibition Our Northern Soul is developed Work is set to begin on a major transformation of Wigan Museum’s ground floor gallery and learning space later this month The redevelopment follows the museum's successful bid for £249k from The National Lottery Heritage Fund This will support the delivery of Our Northern Soul , an ambitious new exhibition that will explore what makes Wigan Borough special through the stories, objects and experiences of local people Wigan Museum will close to the public from Saturday 25 July to enable this work to be carried out, and will reopen in summer 2027 Wigan Local Studies (on the upper floors of the museum) will remain open for much of the redevelopment period while work takes place in the main gallery space
